prompt: Show that the lines $L_1:\ \mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\2\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\2\end{pmatrix}$ and $L_2:\ \mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$ are skew.
markscheme:
Directions are not scalar multiples, so the lines are not parallel **(R1)**

Equate: $1+\lambda=3+2\mu$, $-\lambda=1+\mu$, $2+2\lambda=-\mu$ **(M1)**

From the first two: $\mu=-1$, $\lambda=0$ **(A1)**; third: $2+0=2$ but $-\mu=1$, so $2\ne1$ — inconsistent **(A1)**

Not parallel and not intersecting, so skew **(R1)**

concept: Point of intersection of two lines
